In 2001 the Netherlands became the first country in the world to legalise same-sex marriage. 25 years later, this is how Europe recognises same-sex couples.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The pioneers: Netherlands 2001, Belgium 2003, Spain 2005. Then Norway and Sweden 2009, Iceland and Portugal 2010, Denmark 2012, France 2013, Ireland and Luxembourg 2015, Germany and Finland 2017.
2/ The latest wave: Austria 2019, the whole of the UK 2020, Switzerland and Slovenia 2022, Estonia and Greece 2024.
3/ Yellow means partnerships but no marriage: Czechia 2006, Hungary 2009, Croatia 2014, Cyprus 2015, Italy 2016, Montenegro 2021, Latvia 2024, Lithuania 2025.

4/ Black means no recognition at home, covering most of the Balkans and the east, including Poland, Romania, Bulgaria and Slovakia. 14 European countries define marriage as a man-woman union in their constitutions.

5/ Courts keep moving the line. In 2023 the European Court of Human Rights ruled Poland was violating rights by offering no recognition, and in November 2025 the EU's top court said member states must recognise same-sex marriages concluded elsewhere in the EU.
Marriage, partnerships or neither: where should the line be? Make your case below. Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
